_note: One entry per clause or sub-clause of NMC notice No. R-13014/01/2024-Ethics dated 06/10/2026. 'summary' is a paraphrase, not a quotation. Clause IDs are used everywhere else in the data files and must exist here.

clauses.label: Notice ¶1–2
clauses.title: Public notice: issued with immediate effect
clauses.summary: The cover notice informs all Registered Medical Practitioners and other concerned stakeholders to comply with the annexed Guidelines, and says they come into force with immediate effect.

clauses.title: Commencement
clauses.summary: The Guidelines come into force on the date NMC publishes them.

clauses.title: Preamble and objectives (a)–(f)
clauses.summary: Aims: ethical, truthful, transparent advertising; no false, misleading, exaggerated or unsubstantiated claims; no direct or indirect solicitation or promotion that induces unnecessary tests or treatment; cover digital and emerging technologies; protect patient privacy and autonomy.

clauses.title: Nothing permits what other law prohibits
clauses.summary: These Guidelines do not permit any act that is prohibited under applicable law or the 2002 Regulations.

clauses.title: Definition of “Advertisement”
clauses.summary: Any communication, in any medium, that directly or indirectly solicits or promotes the services, reputation, skills, qualifications, achievements, facilities or commercial services of a doctor or hospital. Digital, social, sponsored, targeted, influencer-led, search-engine, platform-based, audio-visual and AI-generated promotional communication counts where its content or manner of spreading is promotional.

clauses.label: §3.2 Expl. I
clauses.title: Non-promotional public information is exempt
clauses.summary: Sharing information with the public in the normal course, without being promotional and without intent for commercial benefit, is outside the definition of advertisement.

clauses.label: §3.2 Expl. II
clauses.title: Equipment and facilities as factual information
clauses.summary: Information on availability or installation of equipment, technology, diagnostic facilities or services may be shared as fact, provided it has no claims of superiority, guaranteed accuracy, guaranteed outcomes, comparison or other misleading or unverifiable representation.

clauses.label: §3.2 Expl. III
clauses.title: Doctor identity on electronic media posts
clauses.summary: A doctor publishing electronic media posts must transparently disclose their name, qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR registration number.

clauses.label: §3.2 Expl. IV
clauses.title: Clinic must name its doctors on electronic media posts
clauses.summary: A clinical establishment publishing electronic media posts must transparently disclose the names of its doctors with qualifications, registration status and SMR/NMR registration number.

clauses.label: §3.2 Expl. V
clauses.title: Fake, paid or solicited reviews and testimonials
clauses.summary: No doctor or hospital may solicit, purchase, procure, manipulate or cause to be published fake, paid or misleading patient reviews, ratings, testimonials, endorsements or recommendations to promote services. A doctor shall not request or share patient testimonials, recommendations, endorsements or reviews for professional promotion on social media.

clauses.title: Definition of AI
clauses.summary: A self-learning automated process, program, machine or computer built to do tasks that usually need a human brain.

clauses.title: Definition of Hospital / Medical Institution
clauses.summary: A clinical establishment providing facilities for diagnosis, treatment or care, where patients may be admitted or treated as out-patients, in any recognised system of medicine, including institutions covered by the Clinical Establishments Act 2010 or a State Act.

clauses.title: Definition of “Medium of advertisement”
clauses.summary: Includes, but is not limited to, print, TV, radio, social media, websites and blogs, messaging platforms (WhatsApp, Telegram, Facebook etc.), podcasts, influencer marketing, digital marketing campaigns, sponsored posts, AI-generated promotion, public interviews, news articles intended for promotion, online healthcare platforms, and any audio-visual or digital communication.

clauses.title: Definition of Social Media
clauses.summary: All forms of publication and sharing through internet-based websites and apps that let users create, share and join online communities.

clauses.title: Definition of RMP
clauses.summary: Medical practitioners registered under the NMC Act whose names are in the National Register or a State Medical Register.

clauses.title: Applies to professional conduct of RMPs
clauses.summary: The Guidelines apply to the professional conduct of RMPs in advertising, publicity, digital communication and promotional activities.

clauses.title: Read with the 2002 Regulations and NMC Act
clauses.summary: For RMPs the Guidelines are read with the IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002 and the NMC Act 2019. If they cannot be reconciled, the statute and operative regulations prevail.

clauses.title: Read with Clinical Establishments law
clauses.summary: For hospitals and institutions the Guidelines are read with the applicable Clinical Establishments Act or Rules or State Act. If they cannot be reconciled, that Act or those Rules override the Guidelines.

clauses.title: Using an agency does not remove responsibility
clauses.summary: Publishing through a digital platform, third party, advertising agency, influencer or other intermediary does not by itself free a doctor or institution from responsibility for content they authorised, commissioned, sponsored, adopted or knowingly permitted. Consequences are decided by the competent authority under applicable law.

clauses.title: Public health education
clauses.summary: Doctors may take part in awareness programmes, public health campaigns, academic discussions and educational content, provided these do not promote personal practice, do not solicit patients and are not monetised through promotional marketing.

clauses.title: Hoardings and billboards
clauses.summary: Hoardings in public space may be used only to share factual information about infrastructure and facilities. Unverified or unverifiable claims are treated as for commercial gain and are prohibited.

clauses.title: Patient information in advertising needs lawful consent
clauses.summary: Patient information, photographs, videos, records, clinical images, treatment details, testimonials or other identifiable information shall not be used for advertising unless the law permits and the necessary consent and safeguards are in place.

clauses.title: Consent does not legalise a prohibited practice
clauses.summary: Patient consent does not by itself make a testimonial, endorsement, promotional patient story, before-and-after depiction, success claim or other advertising practice permissible if these Guidelines or the law otherwise prohibit it.

clauses.title: Standard for consent
clauses.summary: Where consent is legally required it must be specific, informed, voluntary, documented and capable of verification, and must comply with privacy and data-protection law. The form depends on the law and the purpose of use.

clauses.title: Safeguards even where disclosure is lawful
clauses.summary: Even where disclosure is lawful, the institution and doctor must take reasonable steps to avoid unnecessary disclosure of names and to crop, blur or black out birth marks, identification marks or other identifying information.

clauses.title: Responsible use of social media
clauses.summary: Doctors and clinical establishments should use social media responsibly, balancing public information with patient integrity and professional ethics.

clauses.title: AI-generated promotional content
clauses.summary: An AI-generated promotional campaign for commercial interest is prohibited. AI-generated promotional content that otherwise conforms to the Guidelines, the Regulations and the applicable Clinical Establishments law must carry a source mark that explicitly states the content is AI-generated.

clauses.label: §7.2(a)
clauses.title: No misleading AI content
clauses.summary: AI-generated or AI-assisted content shall not be used to create or spread misleading, deceptive or unverifiable representations about diagnosis, treatment, clinical outcomes, professional qualifications, patient experiences or healthcare services.

clauses.label: §7.2(b)
clauses.title: No synthetic patients, voices or endorsements
clauses.summary: AI shall not be used to create or manipulate a patient's image, testimonial, voice or clinical outcome, or to create a synthetic endorsement or representation purporting to be of an actual patient, doctor or other person.

clauses.label: §7.2(c)
clauses.title: Disclose material AI alteration
clauses.summary: Where AI-generated or materially AI-altered content is used in a way that its artificial nature may reasonably matter to the audience's understanding, appropriate disclosure shall be made.

clauses.label: §7.2(d)
clauses.title: Patient data as AI input
clauses.summary: Any use of patient information as input to an AI system must comply with privacy, confidentiality, data-protection and professional-ethics requirements.

clauses.title: Chapter III governs prohibited practices; government campaigns exempt
clauses.summary: Prohibited practices on advertising, solicitation, endorsements, testimonials, patient images, misleading claims and digital manipulation are governed by Chapter III. An Explanation exempts campaigns on Government of India and State Government programmes and schemes that are in larger public interest.

clauses.title: No identifiable patient data
clauses.summary: Doctors and clinical establishments shall not share patient data, such as names, faces or anomalies, that can be identified publicly.

clauses.title: Live surgery and procedure broadcasts
clauses.summary: Nothing in the Guidelines permits live broadcast or commercial dissemination of surgical or clinical procedures inconsistent with applicable NMC guidelines, directions or advisories. Live surgery broadcasts must follow the NMC framework on patient safety, consent, privacy, educational purpose, sponsorship, commercialisation and professional conduct.

clauses.title: Digital personal data law
clauses.summary: Advertising that involves processing, publishing, storing, disclosing or otherwise using digital personal data must comply, to the extent applicable, with the IT Act 2000 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and Rules made in 2025.

clauses.label: §8.1(i)
clauses.title: No demand creation or fear-based marketing
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not advertise or run activities meant to create unnecessary demand for procedures, promote unnecessary diagnostics, or promote fear-based marketing.

clauses.label: §8.1(ii)
clauses.title: No solicitation, self-promotion or third-party marketing using the doctor's identity
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not solicit patients directly or indirectly, promote services through self-promotion, engage a third party to market medical services, permit use of their name, image, voice, testimonial or endorsement to promote services or products, or join promotional campaigns that give an impression of commercialising practice.

clauses.label: §8.1(iii)
clauses.title: No achievements, success rates, patient numbers or absolute claims
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not advertise personal achievements, professional success rates or number of patients treated, with illustrative assertions such as “Guaranteed cures”, “Best doctors”, “No.1 Specialist”, “100% success”, “painless treatment”, “Miracle treatment”, “Exclusive cure”, or any other unverifiable or exaggerated claim.

clauses.label: §8.1(iv)
clauses.title: No endorsement of drugs, devices or products
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not give, directly or indirectly, any approval, recommendation, endorsement, certificate, report or statement about any drug, medicine, remedy, therapeutic article, apparatus, appliance, medical device, diagnostic or health product for advertising or publicity linked to their name, signature, photograph, voice or professional status, whether or not paid.

clauses.label: §8.1(v)
clauses.title: No cases, surgical results, before-and-after, celebrity patients or success stories
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not publish cases for promotion, advertise surgical results, display before-and-after photographs, publicise celebrity patients or promote personal success stories, unless published strictly for scientific or educational purposes with anonymised patient consent.

clauses.label: §8.1(vi)
clauses.title: No unrealistic expectations, hidden risks or unproven therapies
clauses.summary: A doctor shall not publish statements that create unrealistic expectations, misrepresent outcomes, conceal risks, promote unproven therapies, secret remedies, or treatments whose composition, scientific basis, safety or efficacy is not adequately established or which are otherwise prohibited.

clauses.label: §8.1(vii)
clauses.title: No commissions or lead-generation fees
clauses.summary: No doctor shall offer, pay, solicit, receive or take part in any commission, rebate, bonus, gift, gratuity, referral fee, lead-generation fee or other consideration for promotion or advertisement where it is connected with referral, recommendation or procurement of patients, specimens or materials.

clauses.label: §8.1(viii)
clauses.title: Agency payment must not be tied to individual patients
clauses.summary: Engagement of advertising agencies, digital marketing agencies, influencers or online platforms shall not be structured so that payment or consideration is linked to the procurement or referral of individual patients.

clauses.label: §8.1(ix)
clauses.title: Superiority claims only if objectively verifiable
clauses.summary: No doctor or hospital shall make comparative claims such as “best”, “No.1”, “leading”, “most trusted”, “top”, “number one”, “unmatched” or similar, unless the claim is objectively verifiable, based on a transparent and independently ascertainable methodology, and otherwise lawful.

clauses.label: §8.1(ix) proviso
clauses.title: Awards and rankings must be verifiable
clauses.summary: Any ranking or award used in advertising must be capable of independent verification. Material conditions, methodology, relevant date and details of the awarding organisation or firm must be disclosed where needed to avoid misleading the public.

clauses.label: §8.1(x)
clauses.title: No inducements that encourage unnecessary care
clauses.summary: No doctor or hospital shall use discounts, limited-period offers, contests, coupons, gifts, cashbacks, referral benefits, free procedures or similar inducements in a way that is likely to encourage unnecessary consultation, diagnostic investigation or treatment, or otherwise amounts to solicitation.

clauses.label: §8.1(x) closing line
clauses.title: Fee and package disclosure must be factual
clauses.summary: Any lawful disclosure of charges, packages or fees must be factual, transparent and not misleading.

clauses.label: §8.1(xi)
clauses.title: No celebrity, influencer, patient, employee or third-party endorsements
clauses.summary: No doctor shall use or permit any celebrity, influencer, patient, employee or third party to promote professional services through prohibited testimonials, endorsements or recommendations. Any material commercial relationship in lawful public-health or informational communication must be transparently disclosed. A third party must not be used as an intermediary to do indirectly what the doctor or institution may not do directly.

clauses.label: §8.1(xii)
clauses.title: No fake engagement or search manipulation
clauses.summary: No doctor or hospital shall procure, manipulate or cause a third party to procure or manipulate fake followers, likes, reviews, ratings, testimonials, comments, views or other digital engagement, or manipulate search rankings, visibility or algorithms to create a misleading impression of professional standing.

clauses.label: §8.2(i)
clauses.title: Research-based communication
clauses.summary: Only research-based communication, where the doctor has published case studies in reputed medical journals, is allowed as an exception.

clauses.label: §8.2(ii)
clauses.title: Permitted formal announcements (a)–(g)
clauses.summary: A doctor may make a formal announcement about: starting practice; change of type of practice; change of address; temporary absence from duty; resumption of another practice; succeeding to another practice; public declaration of charge.

clauses.label: §8.2(iii)
clauses.title: Public-health lectures and talks
clauses.summary: Doctors may give lectures or talks on public health and diseases for public awareness on television, radio and electronic media in their own name and designation, without promoting their employer organisation.

clauses.label: §8.2(iv)
clauses.title: Health-education pamphlets for visiting patients
clauses.summary: Doctors may issue health education and general information pamphlets or brochures to patients visiting their clinic or hospital, without claims of superiority over others, unsubstantiated claims or misleading information.

clauses.label: §8.2(v)
clauses.title: Greetings on national or profession-related days
clauses.summary: Doctors may give greetings on days of national importance or related to the medical profession, but these must not contain advertisement of professional gains.

clauses.label: §8.3(i)
clauses.title: What a hospital may publish
clauses.summary: Hospitals may share factual, objective and verifiable information about name, location, contact details, departments, facilities, equipment, services, emergency services, accreditation status, charges and other institutional information permitted by law.

clauses.label: §8.3(ii)
clauses.title: What hospital communication must not contain
clauses.summary: Hospital communication shall not contain patient solicitation, inducement, comparative superiority, guarantees of cure or outcome, unverifiable or exaggerated claims, or promotional portrayal of an individual doctor. The form, medium or frequency must not turn factual information into solicitation or self-aggrandisement.

clauses.label: §8.3(iii)
clauses.title: Stay within the scope allowed by law
clauses.summary: Where advertising is permitted by law, the communication must stay within the scope permitted by that law and these Guidelines.

clauses.title: Clinics: factual information only; doctor directory
clauses.summary: Clinical establishments may advertise only factual, objective and verifiable particulars: name, contact details, departments, diagnostic facilities, emergency services, accreditation status, other facilities and applicable fees. A hospital website directory of doctors (names, recognised qualifications, specialties, registration details, availability) that serves a patient-information function is regarded as distinct from a paid or promotional advertisement.

clauses.title: Doctor's photograph
clauses.summary: Use of a doctor's photograph is not permitted where it amounts to self-advertisement, solicitation or promotional publicity. Self-photographs or similar publicity material on the letterhead or signboard of a consulting room or clinic are governed by Regulations 6.1.1 and 6.1.2 of the 2002 Regulations and regarded as unethical.

clauses.title: Formal announcements: factual and limited
clauses.summary: A doctor may issue formal announcements that are factual, non-promotional and limited to: starting practice, change of address, change of practice type, temporary absence, resumption of practice, and public declaration of consultation fees.

clauses.title: Healthcare platforms
clauses.summary: All healthcare platforms hosting doctors must follow NMC ethical advertising norms, must not rank doctors for payment, and must keep listing practices transparent.

clauses.title: Graded penalties
clauses.summary: The State Medical Council may take action under the NMC Act. Graded action that may be contemplated: first violation, warning and mandatory ethics training; second, censure and monetary penalty; third, suspension of registration for 3–6 months; serious violation (misleading cure claims, inducement of patients, digital mass solicitation), suspension for 6–12 months; repeated violations, removal from the register for 1–3 years.

clauses.label: §10.1 Explanation
clauses.title: Hospitals dealt with under Clinical Establishments law
clauses.summary: Hospitals and institutions engaged in unethical advertising are dealt with under the applicable Clinical Establishments Act and Rules or State Act.

clauses.title: Show-cause notice first
clauses.summary: Penalties are imposed only after a show-cause notice to the doctor and an opportunity to explain.

clauses.title: Reasoned order
clauses.summary: The State Medical Council must issue a reasoned and speaking order setting out the violation, the doctor's contentions and the reasons for the penalty.

clauses.title: First appeal
clauses.summary: A doctor aggrieved by a State Medical Council decision may appeal to the EMRB, NMC within 60 days.

clauses.title: Appellate review
clauses.summary: The Appellate Authority examines the appeal independently and may call for records, direct a fresh assessment or seek additional opinion.

clauses.title: Appellate order
clauses.summary: The Appellate Authority passes a reasoned and speaking order.

clauses.title: Second appeal
clauses.summary: The first appeal decision may be contested by a second appeal within sixty days.

clauses.title: Hospital violations; doctor's personal responsibility
clauses.summary: For a hospital violation the penalty and appeal route under the Clinical Establishments law apply. Where a doctor personally authorised, took part in, endorsed or was otherwise responsible for the prohibited communication, their professional conduct may be separately examined by the State Medical Council, EMRB or NMC.

clauses.title: Power to issue clarifications
clauses.summary: NMC may issue clarifications, advisories, SOPs or procedural instructions consistent with the Guidelines and the NMC Act as needed for effective and uniform implementation.
